newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel says to focus on domestic market.
newsitem.headline: SingTel says to focus on domestic market.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) president Lee Hsien Yang said on Friday the company would give priority to its domestic operations in what is set to be an increasingly competitive local telecoms market.
"Clearly the priority to us is the domestic market," he told reporters after the official opening of a refurbished Singapore $1.6 million SingTel customer service centre.

SingTel's monopoly in telecommunications services in Singapore is in its final days. It will face a rival, MobileOne, in the mobile telephone and pager sector from April 1, 1997 and competition across all sectors by April 1, 2000.
Prospective bidders for the new basic telecoms licences, tender details of which were announced on January 17, have already begun to line up.

Britain's second biggest player, Cable & Wireless has said it will bid for a licence while local firms Singapore Press Holdings and Keppel Corp have entered the cellular market as parters in MobileOne.
Lee said SingTel was looking forward to facing competitors in the market and welcomed "the fact that the regulator wants new operators to come in and build their own infrastructure".
He said SingTel was disappointed it had failed this month in a tender to win licences to enter Taiwan's telecoms market as either a cellular or pager operator.
The Taiwanese government said this month that some 41 groups had bid for eight mobile licences worth S$5.04 billion and 32 applicants had bid for eight pager licences.
"We are sorry to have lost the licence -- we would certainly like to be in the Taiwan market, but I think we will move on and look for other opportunities," Lee told reporters.
He added that new targets for investment in the Asia-Pacific region were also being considered.
